questions.stem: Why must Benedict's solution be heated with the food sample for the test to work?

options.text: Heating dissolves the sugar so it can react
The chemical reaction between Benedict's solution and reducing sugar requires heat energy
Heating kills any bacteria that might interfere with the test
The colour change only occurs when the solution is cold again

questions.explanation: The Benedict's test requires heating because the reaction between the copper sulfate in Benedict's solution and the reducing sugar needs heat energy to proceed.
